Of 1589 records, 111 studies were included after full-text review, hierarchically sorted by validation strategy (prioritizing independent external validation), cohort size, and performance metrics. AI-based prediction has been evaluated across histopathology whole-slide images (WSIs), radiology, omics, endoscopy, clinical variables, and multimodal combinations. Deep learning applied to H&E WSIs is the most extensively studied approach, although external validation remains inconsistent. Multimodal models are promising, but superiority over single-modality models remains unproven. Most studies predict assay-defined MSI/dMMR rather than treatment outcomes; the available evidence does not yet support routine clinical use of AI for triage or assay replacement. Prospective multicenter trials should evaluate AI-derived phenotypes as complementary or standalone biomarkers for treatment selection.

title: Driver gene-based prognostic model benchmarked against machine learning survival models is associated with a CAF–TGFβ–EMT-like phenotype in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is molecularly heterogeneous, limiting conventional prognostic tools. Whole-genome resequencing of six HCC cases was used only to filter candidates. Somatically mutated genes were intersected with HCC-annotated entries from five predefined driver resources, yielding 154 genes. DGPM-HCC, a 13-gene model summarized by TotalScore, was developed in 170 bulk transcriptome samples. In 20 repetitions of event-stratified fivefold cross-validation, DGPM-HCC achieved a mean overall-survival C-index of 0.761; versus continuous Cox13, the median paired ΔC-index was 0.125 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.111–0.142; P = 9.57 × 10 −5 ). The combined nomogram achieved a training-cohort 3-year disease-free-survival AUC of 0.924. External discrimination in TCGA-LIHC was modest (C-index, 0.533; 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs, 0.503, 0.592, and 0.590), whereas GSE14520 lacked three model genes. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing of one tumor–adjacent pair, public single-cell integration, and multiplex immunohistochemistry on 16 specimens associated high TotalScore with a CAF–TGFβ–EMT-like state. Drug-sensitivity findings were computational and exploratory.

title: Prediction of site-specific recurrence and overall survival for colorectal cancer with liver metastases
abstract: Up to 70% of patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) experience recurrence after curative-intent hepatectomy, yet recurrence patterns are heterogeneous across anatomic sites, and no tools currently exist to predict site-specific recurrence dynamically over time. We developed and validated machine learning models to predict overall survival and site-specific recurrence (liver, lung, lymph node, peritoneum) after hepatectomy for CRLM using baseline and dynamic prediction frameworks. In a retrospective cohort of 730 patients who underwent curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLM at the Johns Hopkins Hospital (2000–2024), with a median follow-up of 10.9 years, over 63% of patients experienced recurrence. XGBoost models were trained on clinical, pathologic, and molecular features using nested cross-validation with bootstrap optimism correction. Baseline models achieved C-indices of 0.54–0.67, while dynamic models incorporating surveillance covariates, including adjuvant therapy and interval recurrence at other sites, substantially improved discrimination (C-indices 0.67–0.78; time-dependent AUC 0.68–0.90). Calibration was confirmed with Brier scores of 0.03–0.19. These models enable risk stratification at the time of surgery to inform adjuvant therapy decisions and allow real-time updating of site-specific recurrence risk during follow-up, providing a framework for personalized surveillance strategies in patients with CRLM undergoing curative-intent resection.

title: Decoding drug-tolerant persister states in cancer: insights from single-cell, spatial, and computational approaches
abstract: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have transformed oncogene-driven cancer treatment, but durable responses remain limited by residual disease and acquired resistance. Drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells represent one therapy-surviving component of minimal residual disease (MRD). This Review examines experimental and computational strategies, including patient-derived xenografts, CRISPR screens, single-cell, spatial, multi-omic and artificial intelligence approaches, to define DTP states, MRD heterogeneity, microenvironmental interactions and clinically actionable vulnerabilities with greater resolution in TKI-treated cancers.

title: Decoding spatial mTOR signalling reveals distinct roles in the tumour microenvironment
abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in different tissue compartments influences patient prognosis. We found that mTOR pathway signalling in immune cells correlates with favourable patient survival. Advanced spatially-aware analysis of signalling activities using graph neural networks revealed that the positive association between immune mTOR signalling and patient survival was more pronounced in tumours with features of a more differentiated morphology. Integrative analysis using TCGA data and spatial transcriptomics confirmed a role for immune mTOR signalling in immune activation, accompanied by reduced TGF-β signalling. Our work highlights the importance of adopting a personalised approach to targeting mTOR in cancer patients and establishes a framework for studying cell type-specific signalling in the TME.

title: ANGPTL4 is a hypoxia associated candidate linked to immune and vascular phenotypes in ccRCC
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by prominent vascularization and cellular heterogeneity, but reliable biomarkers for angiogenesis and response to targeted therapy remain limited. In this study, transcriptomic data from GEO cohorts (GSE53757, GSE66271, GSE73731) and two validation datasets (GSE36895, GSE66270) were analyzed using WGCNA and multiple machine learning models. ANGPTL4, together with GPC3, SCARB1, and ADM, was identified as a candidate gene set. ANGPTL4 showed good diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.857) and was positioned between angiogenesis- and lipid metabolism- related modules in the PPI network. Single-cell analysis indicated heterogeneous expression across epithelial and immune cells, and in silico knockout suggested enhanced T-cell–related signaling. ANGPTL4 was identified from a candidate set enriched for hypoxia-related genes and showed cell-type-specific expression in the single-cell dataset. In vitro, ANGPTL4 knockdown altered CCL5 secretion, NK-92-cell-associated phenotypes, and Matrigel network formation. These findings support an association of ANGPTL4 with hypoxia-related, immune, and vascular phenotypes in ccRCC; however, they do not establish direct mediation through the HIF–VEGF signaling axis.

title: LLM-based reconstruction of longitudinal clinical trajectories in chronic liver disease
abstract: Liver cancer primarily develops in patients with chronic liver disease (CLD), yet most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages with poor prognosis. While CLD surveillance generates extensive longitudinal data, its free-text nature hinders large-scale research. To address this, we developed a scalable framework using open-source LLMs with constrained decoding to process unstructured text across radiology, pathology, and transplant assessment domains. A calibration set comprising 507 reports from 30 patients was manually annotated to benchmark four LLMs against a regular expression baseline across 70 tasks. Llama-3.3-70B performed best, exceeding 90% accuracy on 59/70 tasks, outperforming Llama-3.1-8B (a smaller variant), OpenBioLLM-70B (a medically fine-tuned model), and DeepSeek-R1-8B. Constrained decoding achieved > 99.9% format adherence, far surpassing unconstrained prompting (87.4%). Applied to the full cohort, the pipeline analysed 22,493 reports to generate a patient-level database of 29,225 datapoints (35 variables, 835 patients) without manual annotation. Further analysis confirmed known liver cancer risk factors (male sex, viral hepatitis, smoking, diabetes), and allowed for reconstruction of individualised disease timelines. This work provides a scalable blueprint for transforming real-world clinical free-text into structured formats and personalised patient trajectories. Future applications have the potential to accelerate data-driven research into early cancer detection within complex pre-cancerous diseases like CLD.

title: MAVEN: an automated multimodal framework for predicting VETC and early recurrence in HCC
abstract: Accurate identification of aggressive tumor phenotypes remains a major challenge in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Here, we developed and validated MAVEN (Multimodal Automated VETC Estimation Network), a fully automated multimodal deep learning system integrating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs), and clinical variables for predicting vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) and early recurrence risk. In this multicenter study including 1928 patients from five institutions, MAVEN demonstrated superior performance compared with unimodal and bimodal models, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.932 in the internal test cohort and 0.879-0.891 across four independent external cohorts. MAVEN-based risk stratification was significantly associated with early recurrence-free survival across all cohorts. Model explainability analyses revealed that both radiologic and histopathologic features contributed to prediction, with consistent spatial localization of high-risk regions. These findings suggest that multimodal integration enables robust and generalizable prediction of tumor aggressiveness and postoperative risk stratification.

title: Multi-omics integration constructs an inflammation-senescence signature for predicting bladder cancer progression and therapy response
abstract: Bladder cancer (BLCA) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy with significant variability in clinical outcomes. The interplay between inflammation and cellular senescence, referred to as inflammaging, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying inflammaging and its clinical relevance in BLCA remain poorly understood. Inflammaging signature hallmark genes (ISH genes) were identified through correlation analysis using the MSigDB database. A machine learning-based ISH-Riskscore model was developed and validated to predict BLCA prognosis. To explore the biological and clinical relevance of ISH genes and the ISH-Riskscore model, comprehensive analyses were conducted, including functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and drug sensitivity assessments based on multi-omics and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Additionally, the role of SCEL, a key ISH gene, was experimentally validated through functional assays. The ISH-Riskscore model demonstrated robust prognostic performance across multiple independent cohorts. Patients in the low-risk group exhibited higher infiltration of antitumor immune cells, correlating with more favorable clinical outcomes and potentially enhanced responses to immune checkpoint therapy. In contrast, the high-risk group displayed enrichment of pro-inflammatory, invasive, and immunosuppressive pathways, which were associated with poorer survival. scRNA-seq analysis revealed significant upregulation of SCEL in malignant epithelial cells, suggesting its role in tumor progression by promoting proliferation and migration, a finding further validated by in vitro experiments. An inflammaging signature was identified in BLCA, revealing its biological characteristics and clinical relevance. Based on this signature, a novel machine learning-based prognostic model was developed and validated, effectively predicting patient survival and therapeutic responses. Additionally, SCEL was identified as a promising therapeutic target for BLCA management.

title: Network analysis and machine learning approach identifies HSP90-associated synthetic lethal targets and drug responses in breast cancer
abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) is an ATP-dependent molecular chaperone that stabilizes numerous oncogenic proteins involved in proliferation, survival, DNA repair, and therapeutic resistance. Despite its central role in breast cancer (BRCA), monotherapy targeting HSP90 has shown limited clinical success, highlighting the need to identify therapeutically actionable HSP90-associated vulnerabilities. Here, we integrated transcriptomic, network, pharmacogenomic, single-cell, and CRISPR dependency datasets. The major HSP90 isoforms, HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 , were significantly overexpressed in BRCA and independently associated with poor survival. Immune and single-cell analyses linked high HSP90 expression to an immune-cold tumor microenvironment and tumor cell programs related to proliferation, DNA damage response, invasion, and metastasis. Network analysis identified synthetic lethal/viable (SL/SV) interactions involving key regulators, including PAK1, MAP2K1, MAPK3, NFKB1, TNF, CALN1, and HACD3 , highlighting interconnected therapeutic vulnerabilities. Pharmacogenomic integration with GDSC and six machine-learning algorithms identified 26 candidate compounds predicted to be effective across 51 breast cancer cell lines. CRISPR dependency analyses demonstrated negative gene effect scores for HSP90 and several SL partners, supporting their essential roles in tumor cell viability. These findings establish HSP90 as a central regulatory hub and provide a rationale for mechanism-based combination therapies and computational prioritization of precision oncology targets for experimental validation.

title: Machine learning uncovers previously undetectable genetic deletions in cancer panel sequencing
abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild-type by TSO500; 75% (15/20) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and machine-learning analysis of the STAT1–GOLM1 axis in lung adenocarcinoma and small-molecule inhibitor discovery
abstract: Tumor invasion and distant metastasis remain major causes of treatment failure in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), thereby elucidating the molecular mechanisms is critical for precise treatment of LUAD. Using bulk RNA-Seq and single cell transcriptome data, combining with multi-machine learning methods, we identified GOLM1 as a core gene associated with poor prognosis in LUAD, which is highly expressed in malignant epithelial cells characterized by increased extracellular matrix (ECM)-integrin signaling, glycosylation remodelling and invasion-related transcriptional programs. Mechanistically, we validated that STAT1 is an upstream transcription activator of GOLM1 that forms a STAT1-GOLM1 axis that triggers LUAD invasion. Candidate compounds were prioritized by computational molecular docking against STAT1 and subsequently evaluated in A549 cells. Experimental validation revealed that Compound 1 exhibited the strongest inhibitory effect on LUAD cells by regulating PI3K/AKT signaling, cell-cycle and apoptosis. Collectively, our results elucidated the significant role of STAT1-GOLM1 axis in LUAD and provided a promising AI-directed inhibitor for LUAD.

title: Tracking cancer drug resistance with longitudinal multimodal AI: from biological signals to clinical decisions
abstract: Drug resistance remains the dominant cause of therapeutic failure across targeted, cytotoxic, endocrine and immunotherapeutic modalities in oncology. Tumours evolve as heterogeneous ecosystems under treatment pressure, producing branched trajectories that single biomarkers and static baseline assessments capture only incompletely. Digital oncology integrates longitudinal multimodal data—circulating tumour DNA kinetics, serial imaging and radiomics, digital pathology, and real-world clinical streams—with artificial intelligence to model resistance as a dynamic, patient-specific process. This framework supports mechanism discovery, risk stratification, adaptive dosing strategies and biologically informed trial enrichment. Realisation, however, is constrained by incomplete modality availability for individual patients, temporal misalignment between data streams, informative missingness, and the frequent absence of prospective evidence that improved prediction alters management decisions or patient outcomes. This narrative review adopts a use-case-centred structure rather than organisation by modality or algorithm. We examine data foundations that emphasise longitudinal surveillance and lesion-level heterogeneity, fusion strategies designed for missing and asynchronous inputs, and architectures that balance predictive performance with mechanistic interpretability. Applications across therapeutic contexts are evaluated with explicit distinction between retrospective discrimination and demonstrated clinical utility. Evidentiary standards for credible progress—external validation, calibration, missing-modality robustness and decision-impact analysis—are defined, together with governance, equity and regulatory considerations for responsible deployment. The analysis indicates that technical capability is advancing, yet translation requires pragmatic modelling under real-world data constraints and systems that augment rather than replace clinical judgement.

title: Decoding small cell lung cancer vulnerabilities: the AI pathway to next-gen therapeutics
abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is aggressive, treatment-sensitive, and prone to relapse. This Review evaluates how generative AI, graph neural networks, molecular language and diffusion models, structure-based design, and multimodal learning can exploit SCLC dependencies for small-molecule discovery. It integrates biomarker-guided patient stratification, resistance, combination therapy, medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, safety, manufacturing, and clinical translation, emphasizing benchmarked, uncertainty-aware, prospectively validated design–build–test–learn workflows.

title: AI-HistoPS: decoding proteomic heterogeneity with subtype resolution from histopathology in liver metastases
abstract: Liver metastasis is a lethal manifestation of diverse malignancies, but its molecular heterogeneity is not readily captured by routine histopathology. Proteomic profiling has identified functional states of metastatic lesions, although their histomorphological and tumor microenvironmental correlates remain incompletely understood. Here, we developed AI-HistoPS, a computational pathology framework for inferring proteomics-informed states from H&E-stained whole slide images. AI-HistoPS integrates pathology foundation model representations with agent-mediated multiple instance learning to capture subtype-associated morphological patterns. Using multicentre cohorts of liver metastases from multiple primary tumor types, we evaluated associations between histomorphology and three proteomic liver metastasis subtypes (LMS1-3). These states were associated with differences in tumor architecture, stromal composition, and immune cell distribution. AI-HistoPS showed subtype discrimination in the discovery cohort and was evaluated across external cohorts, demonstrating the feasibility of histology-derived representations for proteomics-informed stratification across heterogeneous clinical settings. Attention-guided analyses identified tissue regions associated with subtype-related morphological and microenvironmental features. Multiplex immunohistochemistry supported spatial associations between histological patterns and subtype-related protein markers. These findings suggest that routine histopathology may provide a lower-cost approach for approximating proteomics-informed stratification of liver metastases. Further validation in larger, more diverse, prospectively collected cohorts is required before clinical implementation or use in prognostic or treatment-related decision-making.
